Title: Organization mode — one member's order advances the SHARED mission progress every colleague reads
Preconditions: Store {{STORE_ID}} is in Organization mode — the store setting Loyalty.LoyaltyBalanceCalculationMode reads "Organization". This is NOT the ambient state of the environment (the platform default is "Customer", which the rest of the loyalty corpus assumes), so the run sets it before this suite and restores it after; a case here that finds the store in Customer mode must report BLOCKED rather than assert. THE TARGET IS @td(ORG_LOY_MISSION_PARTIAL.id) — Published, OrderCountGoal count @td(ORG_LOY_MISSION_PARTIAL.goal_count), reward @td(ORG_LOY_MISSION_PARTIAL.reward), targeted at the customer group @td(ORG_LOY_MISSION_PARTIAL.target_group), which the seeder keeps equal to the outlet's membership, and minted fresh per run by npm run seed:org-loyalty. IT MUST BE UNCONSUMED, AND IT MUST NOT BE THE COUNT-1 MISSION. Mission progress is TERMINAL per owner and this build has no reset path (/api/loyalty-mission-progress is search+get and nothing else), so a count-1 target is Completed the instant anything accrues and every later read then compares two values that were already pinned before the case acted — the case PASSES without observing anything. That is exactly what happened on 2026-09-16: the count-1 mission had been completed by an earlier lane 67 minutes before this case ran, both reads returned the same terminal value, member A placed a real order and nothing moved, and the verdict was vacuous. A count-2 target leaves ONE order at 1 of 2 — still InProgress, still movable — so the follow-up read is a measurement rather than a re-read of a frozen row. The guard assertions below make a target that is already non-zero, already Completed, or absent from the member's list report BLOCKED rather than pass; a re-run therefore needs a freshly seeded mission (node scripts/seed-data/loyalty/seed-org-loyalty.mjs --missions-only --only ORG_LOY_MISSION_PARTIAL). LIMIT: the module offers only UserGroupIsCondition and AnyUserGroupCondition, so there is NO organization-native mission targeting on this build — audience == org membership is an equivalence THIS FIXTURE maintains, not one the product guarantees, and nothing here concludes anything about org-native targeting. LIMIT: a promotion adds a gift line (isGift true, price 0) to every order placed on the seeded earn products, so nothing here counts cart lines or pins an order total.

Only a funded pool separates the two, which is why the unlocked control read is taken in the same minute and why a zero control makes this case BLOCKED rather than green. A loyalty balance CANNOT be reset on this platform — vc-module-loyalty exposes the operation log read-only, with no balance set/debit API and no reversal path (BL-LOY-019) — so every balance figure below is a RELATIVE DELTA against a value read immediately before the action, never an absolute number.

Title: Organization mode — a buyer with no organization spends points earned BEFORE the mode flip, and the debit lands on the same balance they were shown
Preconditions: Store {{STORE_ID}} is in Organization mode — the store setting Loyalty.LoyaltyBalanceCalculationMode reads "Organization". This is NOT the ambient state of the environment (the platform default is "Customer", which the rest of the loyalty corpus assumes), so the run sets it before this suite and restores it after; a case here that finds the store in Customer mode must report BLOCKED rather than assert. @td(LOY_PERSONAL_NOORG.email) belongs to NO organization and holds a loyalty balance strictly above @td(LOY_PERSONAL_NOORG.cheapest_pts_price) — the seeder guarantees that floor, which is what makes a refusal to spend attributable to the scope split and never to a genuine shortfall. THE POINTS ARE STRANDED, AND THAT IS THE POINT: the flip from Customer to Organization mode is a measured no-op on existing data. The ledger read immediately before and immediately after the flip on 2026-09-16 was byte-identical at 33 rows, signed sum 128,593, every row carrying organizationId null, so a pre-flip balance stays keyed to the USER while the store now resolves balances by ORGANIZATION. This case asks whether that stranded money is still spendable end to end. WHY THIS IS NOT LOYORG-001 RESTATED: both cases now assemble the SAME mixed cart and both reach order creation — LOYORG-001 Steps were repaired during this run to add a cash line from @td(LOY_SKU_PRIORITY.sku) before the points line, for exactly that reason, so the earlier claim that it cannot reach order creation no longer holds and is not the differentiator to read. THE DIFFERENTIATOR IS THE SETTLEMENT HALF, which LOYORG-001 does not assert at all: it stops at a returned order number, while this case reads the balance and the ledger back AFTERWARDS and requires bal_after below BAL_BEFORE and hist_after totalCount above HIST_BEFORE. That is what proves the points actually MOVED rather than merely that checkout was permitted, and it proves the debit landed on the SAME user-keyed ledger the pre-flip stranded rows sit in — the question this case exists to answer. An order created against an unmoved balance PASSES LOYORG-001 and FAILS this case, which is why both rows are worth their cost. SHARED IRREVERSIBLE COST, STATED BECAUSE THE TWO ROWS ARE NOT INDEPENDENT: LOYORG-001 and this case both place a real order and both burn points from @td(LOY_PERSONAL_NOORG.email), whose balance cannot be restored by any path — the operation log is read-only, there is no balance set or debit API, and no reversal exists (BL-LOY-019). EACH of them must therefore re-verify that balance above @td(LOY_PERSONAL_NOORG.cheapest_pts_price) before every repeat run, and neither may assume a floor established before the other ran. A loyalty balance CANNOT be reset on this platform — vc-module-loyalty exposes the operation log read-only, with no balance set/debit API and no reversal path (BL-LOY-019) — so every balance figure below is a RELATIVE DELTA against a value read immediately before the action, never an absolute number. STATED FIXTURE LIMIT: every execution spends points from @td(LOY_PERSONAL_NOORG.email) and there is no way to give them back, so the balance must be re-verified above @td(LOY_PERSONAL_NOORG.cheapest_pts_price) before each repeat run.
